all_reforms_including_excluded.description: Japan maintained tax incentives and support mechanisms for labour-saving and technology-enhancing investment in manufacturing and service industries, recognizing that persistent labour shortages create ongoing motivation for R&D-related equipment investment and productivity-enhancing capital spending.
all_reforms_including_excluded.package_name: Labour Shortage Response and Productivity Enhancement (1993)
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: Tax incentives for technology-enhancing investment directly support productivity growth and capital deepening in response to labour market constraints, raising potential output per worker.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: Text states 'Japan maintained incentives', indicating ongoing implementation.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: Maintenance of existing incentive scheme rather than a new or substantially reformed instrument; incremental policy continuity.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: A characteristic of manufacturing investment during the boom was the increasing weight of R&D-related and labour-saving equipment investment. With the labour shortage likely to persist in the long run, the incentive to make labour-saving and technology-enhancing investment continues to be strong.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The description focuses on tax incentives for 'labour-saving and technology-enhancing investment' but does not explicitly mention R&D funding or knowledge transfer mechanisms.

all_reforms_including_excluded.description: The April 1993 fiscal package allocated ¥1.15 trillion for investment in education, research and social welfare facilities as part of a broader public infrastructure spending programme.
all_reforms_including_excluded.package_name: April 1993 Public Infrastructure and Social Investment Package
all_reforms_including_excluded.growth_orientation_rationale: Investment in research infrastructure and education facilities supports long-term productivity growth and human capital accumulation, enhancing innovation capacity.
all_reforms_including_excluded.status_evidence: Text describes the April 1993 fiscal package as an allocation decision, indicating legislative passage but implementation status not explicitly confirmed as complete.
all_reforms_including_excluded.importance_rationale: Significant infrastructure investment programme with substantial budget allocation (¥1.15 trillion), but part of a broader counter-cyclical fiscal package rather than a structural reform of the research system.
all_reforms_including_excluded.source_quote: In addition to general public works (Y 7.67 trillion), the infrastructure spending incorporated Y 1.15 trillion for investment in education, research and social welfare facilities.
all_reforms_including_excluded.cross_verification_note: The reform is part of a broader 'public infrastructure spending programme' and does not clearly indicate a direct focus on R&D funding or research infrastructure relevant to the OECD criteria.
